what_this_is: AlphaVox's voice, measured from AlphaVox's own 26 recorded phrases, for christman_synth (christman_sound.voice_profile applies it). The recordings are AlphaVox's voice and no one else's. Every value sits beside the measurements it came from.
applied: F0 median and pitch contour -> per-phone pitch; rate -> christman_synth's rate; each measured vowel's F1, F2, F3 -> that vowel's formant targets. Not applied, and why: the measured bandwidths (christman_sound.formants says LPC bandwidths read far too narrow when F1 sits on a harmonic, and a too-narrow bandwidth would make the synthesizer ring), consonants (their places inside a word cannot be told apart from word times alone), and vowels in not_measured. Those keep Codec War's table values. Added 2026-10-28: each gliding vowel in glides (onset and offset F1-F3, measured from at least MIN_TOKENS_TO_APPLY tokens) -> the glide christman_synth_clear draws across that vowel, onset to offset, in place of the single vowel row.

aligner.phrase_text: from the file name; a phrase whose decoded words differ is left out
aligner.run_to_run: word times on the same file move by up to one 30 ms frame between runs (measured 2026-10-28: 3 to 4 of 26 phrases; one vowel's F3 moved 10 Hz, one contour point 0.06 semitones, over three runs)

f0.source: median F0 of every voiced frame (christman_yin inside christman_sound.formants) over all aligned recordings

pitch_contour.source: each phrase cut into 5 equal parts between its first word's start and last word's end; each part = median semitones of its voiced frames from that phrase's own F0 median; value here = median across phrases. Applied at each phone's centre, straight lines between the points.

rate.source: per phrase: the synthesizer's own duration for the words at rate 1.0 (Codec War table, position and mapping factors, 0.08 s gaps) / the recorded duration of the same words (Vosk: first word start to last word end); value = median over phrases
